data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2023 were GBP 3,045.2m. During 2023 gross prior-period reserves reduced by GBP 1,271.2m (a ~41.8% reduction of opening reserves) driven principally by the 2023 RiverStone reinsurance-to-close and quota share transactions which transferred large amounts of discontinued business, together with favourable claims development and lower catastrophe losses in 2023. The release materially reduced technical claims provisions across multiple lines, notably motor and third party liability where prior RiverStone activity had concentrated, and improved the Syndicate's underwriting position.
raw_causal_phrases: During 2023, prior period reserves were reduced by GBP 25.3 million (2022: strengthened by GBP 34.6 million), representing a reduction of 1.9% of the claims ratio (2022: increase of 3.3% to the claims ratio).

The movements arising from prior year claims line above includes movements relating to RiverStone contracts entered into during the current and prior year, with the movements explained further in note 4.
The 2023 RITC related to GBP 930.0 million of net reserves and is the largest third party RITC in the history of Lloyd's.
natural catastrophes generated losses to the Syndicate totalling GBP 40.3 million (3.0% of the loss ratio), the most material being the Turkey earthquake and Hawaii wildfires.
Ukraine claims had impacted the 2022 loss ratio by 9.1%, with no equivalent in 2023 as we maintained reserving levels set in 2022.

data.data_quality_notes: Primary gross opening reserves taken from Balance Sheet (Technical provisions: Claims outstanding). Prior-year development taken from Note 12(a) 'Movements arising from prior year claims' (gross insurance liabilities). These movements are materially distorted by the 2023 RiverStone RITC and Quota Share transactions (see Note 4) which transferred large discontinued reserves off the Syndicate balance sheet; narrative net prior-period reserve figures (e.g. a GBP 25.3m reduction) differ from the gross movement due to reinsurance and the RITC transfers. The claims development triangle is available and was used as a cross-check; RITC activity means some tables are distorted and interpretation should consider the RITC disclosures.
